## What this phase is for

**Volume 07 is fifty chapters on fifty days, one chapter to one day, days 301 to 350, and it is closed. Its outline was written by the second phase in this repository that was permitted to decide anything, it took four decisions, and they are in `outline/series.md` under *DECISIONS OF RECORD, VOLUME 07* in that file's own words. Read them before you read anything else, because every one of them is load-bearing for the record you are about to write and one of them — the volume's line — was struck and replaced and the price of that is written down.**

`state/volume-06-close.md` is the model and `state/volume-05-close.md` is the closer one. A batch summary is about a batch; a close record is about a volume and is the one page a writer reads before planning anything.

**This volume needs its close record for one reason more than the last four did, and the reason is that this is the first volume in this repository in which something was taken back off a page and cannot be put on one again.**

**ON DAY 342, IN A ROOM OVER A MARKET, IN DAYLIGHT, WITH A DATE IN CHALK ON THE DOOR, A MAN OF ABOUT THIRTY-FOUR WHO KEEPS A STALL TOOK A WORD OFF THE REGISTER-KEEPER'S SECOND SLATE WITH A CLOTH, AND THE WORD HAD BEEN PUT ON THAT SLATE THIRTY-TWO DAYS EARLIER IN THE SAME room AND IN DAYLIGHT AND WITH A DATE ON THE DOOR, AND IT WAS THE ONLY PAGE IN FOUR HUNDRED MILES THAT HAD IT, AND AFTER THAT IT IS ON NO PAGE IN THE WORLD AND NO PAGE IN THE WORLD WILL EVER CARRY IT AGAIN.** By the last page of the volume, a straight line in an orchard has no name on anything, and the reader knows what it was called, and nobody in four hundred miles can say so out loud. **That is a state no earlier volume of this book has been in, and a close record that does not say it plainly has missed the volume.**

### 1. Write `state/volume-06-close.md`'s successor: `state/volume-07-close.md`

**It does not exist. This phase creates it. Do not create a batch prompt of any kind, do not create a continuation directory, do not create a Volume 08 prompt of any kind, and do not create a review prompt. The next phase, whatever it turns out to be, is whatever you make it be at the end of this run, and you make it at the end of this run and not before.**

Read `state/volume-06-close.md` and `state/volume-05-close.md` in full first and copy their shape and not their content. Every part of the record is already written somewhere and has to be gathered, compressed and not invented:

- **A single opening paragraph that puts a reader in the last scene of the volume**, with a day number, a weekday, a date form, an hour and a place. **Volume 07 ends on day 350, a Monday by the founding rule and derived from day 1 being a Tuesday, the thirty-fifth day of the Bare Month, a month with no registered length at all, at about the seventh hour of the morning at the top of a shut road: a man of about sixty with a handcart and a length of rope that has been used and is not new is putting in the tenth of ten willow posts he has cut himself in a copse about four miles the other way, and he began at a row of trees because a row of trees is a thing you can see from a road, and he did not measure anything, and about four feet is a number he has in his mouth and not a number he took off anything, and a man of about fifty-seven who bought half a holding about forty years ago is standing in the road with a hand flat on the second post the way a man does to a gate post, and a man of about thirty-one who carries things for a living came up with nothing in his hands and is not going to be asked anything, and a mark in a field about four feet behind the fence has no word on it anywhere in the world and never will have one again.** Nine or ten sentences. It is the inheritance and it must be readable alone.
- **§1 What Volume 07 answered.** Gather it from the five batch records and check it against the chapters, because a batch record is a witness and not a court. **The honest answer is short and should be written short: a boundary that could only be settled by a page four hundred miles away, and four people who could fetch it and were never asked; a month named on a page by a notary who said the cost out loud first and declined to give it a length, and a hinge that had to fall inside the first twenty days or thirty-five chapters would have had no form to write a date in; five sheets that went out in five hands in five days with four days of notice and nothing at the top of any of them; a woman of about twenty-one who stopped waiting to be told what she is for; a woman of about sixty-one who said no in four words before anybody asked her; a man who paid for half a holding and is right; a man of about fifty-two who would look at a line from the end of it and would not put his hands on it, and did, and learned nothing; a rule about words on a wall, refused out loud in about four seconds by a man who had put a person on a board and taken them off it; a word put to a line in the ground and taken back off the only page it was ever on, in a cloth, by the man who said it; a line entered in a register as one that may not be dug; and a fence four feet off it that a man nobody sent put up on a shut road.**
- **§2 What Volume 07 deliberately did not answer.** All of it, and it is not a gap: **the boundary, which is not settled and is recorded as a refusal;** the day-154 sentence, which is the moral centre of the volume and is on a page in Volume 03 and Volume 04 and is not repeated in any of the fifty; the ninth line and whether it works, and its author is on no roster in this city at his own request; the four people who have not left, 205 days at day 350 and derived and on no page and in no mouth; the two rolls of the same gates, put side by side by nobody, and a keeper is not a holder and the word is at zero; the nineteen stones and the eight that are different and the order they were in; a woman of forty-eight in a fourth house at Nine Elms; the girl of seventeen; the keeper of the Redroot gate, whose year is not named and whose days are not counted; the room at the far end of the Narrow Mark; the boards under the chapel; the eight names at the foot of a hundred-and-forty-year-old page; the island; the box; the Crown's schedule, which stands and is correct and is never opened; the Regent, who is nine hundred miles away and is not defeated and whose one correct sentence still costs the Marches the winter road and costs the Crown nothing; and the man of about thirty-one on the bank, who is on a page sixteen times and is in no chapter of this volume.
- **§3 What is live into whatever comes next.** **Eight to twelve items, chosen because the next volume's plan needs them and not because they are the most interesting.** The obvious ones: **a line in an orchard with no word on any page in the world, which is the first time this book has spent a word and cannot get it back;** an entry in a register that says a straight mark in a field may not be dug, with a day on it and nothing under the day and the third column left empty on purpose, and a shelf with a slate on it with a date on it and nothing under it; the man of about fifty-seven, who has a line he cannot show anybody, a winter he cannot get back, a rope he has never used and a fence four feet off something; the man of about fifty-two and his one sentence that is not an answer, which is on no page; the man of about thirty-four and the ninth line and six refusals; the man of about twenty-five's nine words in a coat; three of the four who will go and a fourth who will not; a woman of about twenty-one with a cut-down pen; the woman of about sixty-nine's sheet in a room and not in a book; the question she asked on the thirty-first and nobody answered; the shut road and the fence; the boards off the wall and the bare wall; the store's board, unwritten since day 225; the man who trades on a board and the place where a name was; the keeper at a shut gate who has not been asked anything. **Say in the record which items you dropped and why, because a close record that silently drops is a close record nobody can check.**
- **§4 What must not be re-litigated.** The standing prohibitions, carried and compressed: **the sixth form, *the Nth day of the Bare Month*, the Nth being the day less 315, established on a page in Chapter 0316 by Sera Vail after a refusal whose reason was the refuser's, with NO LENGTH STATED, and that is the cheapest protection the volume bought and a chapter that ends a month by declaring it over has thrown it away for a small effect;** **NO CHAPTER MAY USE AN ORDINAL FOR A MONTH, and this is forward-looking from day 301 and applies to every volume after this one**; that a weekday is a figure and day 1 is a Tuesday and every one of the fifty was recomputed from that and eleven faults of the family *a correct weekday attached to the wrong sentence* were found in the last ten days and repaired; the volume's one panel, spent on day 340, and that the wall said nothing on the other forty-nine days and on all ten days of the last batch; that the count of this city's silences is derived, on no page, in no mouth, and is **240 at day 340 and 250 at day 350** and is printed in no chapter; that a bolded speech is the only speaker marker in the manuscript; that a narrative paragraph is never in bold; **that the day-154 sentence — *a page with a person's name in it is a description, and a description is a removal with a column for where the person is* — is not said, restated, paraphrased, improved on or put into a second mouth in any of the fifty chapters and is the moral centre of the volume and is on a page in an earlier one**; **and that the word on the second slate is on a page once in Chapter 0310, in narration twice in Chapter 0342, in no mouth at all, and at zero in the other forty-seven files, and no file this phase produces may print it.**
- **§5 The one thing the next phase should know about the shape of the book.** Write it in the voice of the person handing it over. **Nobody in fifty days got stronger.** Adrian Vale is Stage 2 on all fifty days, performed no working, no threshold was opened, the Narrow Mark is not opened a third time, the other world is not named once across the fifty files, nobody offered him a workway and he asked for none, and the words *passage* and *privilege* are at zero. **He is named in ONE of the volume's last ten chapters, Chapter 0346, and in no chapter in any form in the other nine, and the one is a room in which he is reading a page, and the rule that he is named in the chapters where he reads a page and is in no chapter in the chapters where people decline to ask him is the finding of Volume 06's close record and this volume showed it nine times instead of asserting it.** The gains are a month with a name and no length, a name read off an index in four seconds and not put on anything, five sheets in five hands with nothing at the top of them, a yes nobody asked for, nine words nobody has said, eight of nineteen stones and nobody able to say when, a skylight, a door nobody turned a person out at, a refusal of the only page that would have worked, four doors in a row and not one person who can say where their own ground stops, a second bar on no roll, a rule about words, a name off a board, a word put to a line in the ground and taken back off the only page it was ever on, a sentence that is not an answer, a line that may not be dug, nine boards off a wall, and a fence. **None of them is a power. One of them is the price of a power. All of them are heavier than a power.**
- **§6 The new question, in the volume's own words and in a mouth.** `outline/volume-07.md` §13: **what is a person for, on a page, when the only thing anybody needs them for is a journey.** It is asked once, on the thirty-first day of the Bare Month, in a room, in daylight, with a date on the door, by the woman of about sixty-nine who holds a folded sheet thirty years old in a tin, and **it is not answered, and four of the nine people in that room had an answer and four of them said nothing, and the answer four of them had was a column, and a woman who keeps that book had left the third column empty on purpose about four hours earlier.** It is the first time this book has asked what a page is *for* about a person who is useful rather than a person who is at risk. Record that it is asked, where, by whom, in what words, and that nothing answered it.

### 2. The four decisions this phase takes, and where they go

**A close phase is the only phase in this repository after an outline phase that is allowed to decide anything, and it takes four, and it writes all four in `outline/series.md` under a new heading *DECISIONS OF RECORD, VOLUME 08* in your own words, the way the Volume 07 outline phase wrote its four and the way Volume 06's close phase wrote its four. Read `outline/series.md` first and match the shape exactly, including where the heading goes relative to the Volume 07 block.**

The four are:

1. **THE VOICE OF THE NEXT VOLUME, confirmed or not, and if it is confirmed say so in a sentence and say what carries.** Volume 06's close record confirmed Volume 05's and Volume 07's outline confirmed Volume 06's: **fifty-day volumes, one chapter to one day, about a page and a yard and a wage in salt.** Nobody gets stronger. **And add to it whatever this volume found about the shape of the sentence, because the finding is that the narrator's one counting habit and the bolded speech are both instruments that want a person in a room, and the six chapters of the last ten that had an object or a road for a subject ran at 7.1 to 10.4 per cent bolded against the three that had a room at 9.3 to 11.6.** That is a finding about a batch and not about the voice, and a volume that writes a higher share of objects will publish a lower mean for reasons that have nothing to do with quality.
2. **THE LINE OF THE NEXT VOLUME, and it must be audited before it is adopted.** `outline/volume-07.md` §19 records the standing test and it is the one that matters: **a line is made of words the manuscript has never used and of things the manuscript has never seen, and a line that is only the first is a line that collides with a page that already means something else.** Volume 07's incoming line was struck for exactly that reason and four of its nouns collided. **Audit the next line the same way Volume 07's was audited, on the fifty files and not on a state file, and publish the count.**
3. **THE CALENDAR OF THE NEXT VOLUME, and this is the one that cannot be skipped.** `bible/power-system.md` §33A item 2 records that **the Bare Month was registered with no span at all**, and a chapter may write an ordinal for any day of it and no chapter may say what the month does at its end, how many days it has, or whether it is long or short, **and a later volume that needs a sixth month form may not assume this one has sixty days in it or a hundred.** **So the next volume begins on an unknown number of days into a month of no stated length, and that is a decision the close phase has to take deliberately and not by accident, and it has to be written in `bible/power-system.md` as a new numbered section in the same numbered form as §33A and not as an amendment of §33A.** If the next volume is a fifty-day volume, say what the day numbers are and what the form is and whether the Bare Month ends inside the volume, and **if it does, the end of it is a thing on a page in a room in daylight with a date on it by a person, and not a sentence in a state file and not a chapter that guesses.**
4. **THE CAST, and the rule that no name and no place arrives by narration.** Volume 06's state layer broke this by naming a gatekeeper who was on no page and a review caught it, and the name is in the repository only as the record of the strike. **Decide who the next volume puts on a page and by what instrument, and say the instrument, and the instrument this repository has is the oldest one in the book: a document arrives and is read out.**

### 3. The interval figure in the plan layer, and it is the one thing a batch could not fix

**`outline/volume-07.md` §13 says the word was on a slate *for sixteen days*. IT WAS ON IT FOR THIRTY-TWO.** Day 310 to day 342, both at about the fourth hour of the afternoon, and every use in Chapters 0342 and 0343 is thirty-two with both anchors named in the same sentence, and the finding is in `state/batch-summaries/volume-07-batch-0005.md` §9 and in `state/continuity.md` and `state/open-threads.md`. **A figure that comes out at exactly half of the right one is the signature of a subtraction taken across the wrong boundary, and this is the largest single class of fault in this repository, and it is born in outlines, and Volume 07's own §33A item 8 exists because of it.**

**A batch routed it and did not settle it and a batch may not settle it. This phase settles it, because this phase may decide, and the amendment belongs to `outline/volume-07.md` §13 and nowhere else. Make the edit, say in the record that you made it, and give the arithmetic in the record in full so that a later writer can check it in one line.**

### 4. The two open figures the volume carried without settling, and what this phase does with them

1. **The age of the man who trades on the Open Hand board.** `outline/volume-07.md` §6.4, §17.8 and §17.10 say **a man of about thirty-seven**; Chapter 0309 of this volume says **about thirty-seven**; **the prose of Volumes 02 to 06 says about thirty-nine at eighteen named chapters**, and he is in none of the fifty chapters of this volume with an age on him. **They are the same man. Decide which figure is right, amend the losing side, and record the decision. This phase is permitted to decide it and a batch was not, and leaving it open is a decision to leave it open and that is the worst of the three available.**
2. **The fact that the fourth of the four said no on the fourteenth of the Bare Month in a room with a date on the door, in four words, before anybody asked, and that the room on the eighteenth is Chapter 0333, in which she came to the door and did not come in, and that nobody in this volume is going to ask her about it.** **That is not a figure and it is not to be softened and it is not a defeat and nobody may soften it. Carry it forward whole and say in the record that it is carried whole.**

### 5. The measurements, republished with their definitions, and the two that are worse than the batches before them

**Publish the definition or publish nothing. A figure a later writer will quote is worth less than a figure with the instrument printed beside it, and the two figures below are worse than the four batches before them and have to be published as they stand and not as they would look.**

- **The share of words inside bold marks, on Volume 07's last ten files: 7.1 to 11.6 per cent, a mean of 9.3, in forty-seven spans, and the longest bolded turn is eighty-nine with about 90 the working ceiling and ninety-five the hard one and no turn over either.** Against Batch 0004's 8.9 to 19.8 with a mean of 13.9, Batch 0003's 7.0 to 18.4 with a mean of 13.4, Volume 06's 6.2 to 21.8 with a mean of 13.8, Volume 01's 10.4 as the model and about 35 as the ceiling. **The mean is four and a half points below the four batches before it and the cause is named in the batch record and in `bible/power-system.md` §45 item 9.**
- **The exchange, on the published definition — a plain speech is a paragraph carrying a quotation mark and no bold mark, answered when the very next non-blank paragraph carries a quotation mark and a bold mark — is 134 plain speeches and 27 answered at twenty point one per cent, against Batch 0004's 16 of 28 at fifty-seven per cent. The instrument reproduces Batch 0004's published figure exactly on Batch 0004's own ten files, so the difference is in the files and not in the script, and the denominator is four and a half times Batch 0004's because the last ten days of this volume carry far more speech than the four batches before them, and the rate falls because the four-speech-paragraph ceiling puts a narration paragraph between exchanges.** A number is a consequence and not a plan.
- **The chorus frame, on the bare head every occurrence of *about four people in*: seventy-seven in four hundred and forty-three paragraphs on the last ten files, one in five point seven, against one in three point seven in Batch 0004, one in three in Batch 0002, one in about five in Batch 0001 and one in about four across Volume 06. This is the fourth batch running in which the figure has improved and it is the best in the volume, and it is at zero in three of the last ten files.**
- **The word-run, and the two instruments that must not be compared.** On a sequential token match across all fifty files with each lead paragraph subtracted, the top run is **twelve**. Batch 0004's published top was **fifty-five** on a longest-common-substring. **These are two instruments and two numbers and the record has to say so, because a later writer who sets them side by side will draw a conclusion about duplication that is not there.** What the figure does say is that the last ten days share no long verbatim run with each other or with any earlier file.
- **And the two standing repairs a later writer must not trip over.** A **stray quotation mark is at nineteen lines in Chapters 0281 to 0290 and is still unrepaired and still belongs to a Volume 07 review-repair pass**, and **the forty-word near-duplicate sentence across the 0254 and 0262 boundary is still unrepaired**, and neither is visible to any check that runs inside a batch.

**At the end of this run, look at what the record says is still live and create exactly one next-phase directory and its prompt. Do not create a second one. Do not create a review prompt, a continuation directory, a batch prompt and a close prompt both, or any Volume 08 anything that the four decisions have not earned.**

**The next phase is whatever §2's four decisions have made it, and in this repository that has been an outline phase, and if it is, then the prompt is an outline prompt for the volume those four decisions describe, and it must carry the same three things every outline prompt in this repository carries: the four decisions as this phase wrote them and not as summaries of them, the audit of the line before the line is adopted, and the calendar question at §2 decision 3 with the Bare Month's missing length in it in full, because that is the one a later volume gets wrong by not noticing it.**

**And the inheritance paragraph at the end of that prompt is the one a writer actually reads, and it has to be readable alone, and it has to end on the fence and on the fact that the word is off the page and cannot go back on it.**
